text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi denies rumours circulating over the need for additional deficit cutting measures other than those presented in the 1997 budget: "this budget will be enough to bring the public deficit down to 3 pct of GDP in 1997" (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi says he is not held hostage by hard-left party leader Fausto Bertinotti. "This is the budget of the whole government, of the whole coalition. Bertinotti is not in charge" (Corriere della Sera).

* EU commissioner Mario Monti says in an interview Italy should "understand once and for all that the country is likely to die if it stays out of Europe, but not if it follows a slimming diet to get in" (La Repubblica).
* The opposition centre-right Freedom alliance wants to present a "counterbudget" and announces street demonstrations against the government (all).
* Bank of Italy Governor Antonio Fazio says he is not going to cut interest rates because the inflation rate is not under control yet (La Stampa).
* Finance minister Vincenzo Visco says the special "tax for Europe" on revenues will have a impact "between zero and two million lire" (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
